stem: Ravi starts facing North. He turns 90 degrees clockwise, then walks 5 km. He then turns 90 degrees clockwise again and walks 3 km. Which direction is he now facing?

per_option_rationale.rationale: North -> turn 90 CW -> East -> turn 90 CW -> South. Ravi faces South after two clockwise 90-degree turns from North.
Applying only the first clockwise turn (North -> East) and ignoring the second turn gives East.
Turning counter-clockwise instead of clockwise from North gives West, omitting the correct turn direction.
Counting two 90-degree turns as a full 360-degree rotation returns the person to North, an arithmetic slip on cumulative angle.

explanation: Starting North, each 90-degree clockwise turn shifts: North -> East -> South. After two such turns Ravi faces South.

explanation_sections.punchline: Two consecutive clockwise quarter-turns from North land you facing South.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: track facing direction after each turn. Turn 1: North + 90 CW = East. Turn 2: East + 90 CW = South. Distance walked is irrelevant to the final facing direction.
explanation_sections.lesson: Each 90-degree clockwise turn advances facing direction by one step in the sequence N -> E -> S -> W -> N.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 30 seconds. The trap is confusing clockwise with counter-clockwise at the second turn, landing on West.
